name: Greenhouse
tagline: Enterprise hiring platform with structured interviewing.
description: Greenhouse is recorded as an enterprise hiring platform built on structured interviewing, where interview kits and scorecards feed a handoff to the HRIS.
pros: Structured interview kits and scorecard-based evaluation are the capabilities our own guides attach to this class of hiring tool, keeping every interviewer on the same rubric
Reporting on source quality and time-to-hire arrives with the platform per our HR technology guide, so recruiting spend can be read against where candidates actually came from
The onboarding handoff is described concretely in our glossary: an accepted offer starts IT provisioning, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment in the HRIS without a manual relay
It holds the number two spot in our recruiting software ranking, and our small-team question names it first among the entry points buyers typically start with
Ten head-to-head records give it five wins, including the category pairings against Lever, Workday, and Zoho People
cons: Our HR category page prices recruiting-specific tools on annual contracts while this page carries a monthly band, so the recorded unit for Greenhouse's price disagrees with itself
It is a hiring layer rather than the employee record: our guides assume a separate HRIS receives the handoff, leaving payroll and core HR to another vendor

content.title: Where Greenhouse sits in a hiring stack
content.body: Our records place Greenhouse as an enterprise hiring platform built around structured interviewing, and our HR technology guide treats it as the dedicated applicant tracking system a company graduates to once hiring volume outgrows a lightweight tool. In that framing Greenhouse is not the system of record for employees. It runs requisitions through to accepted offers and then hands off: the same guide names the handoff into the HRIS as the key integration point, which is why our onboarding glossary describes platforms of this type triggering onboarding workflows the moment an offer is accepted.

content.title: Interview kits and scorecards
content.body: The capabilities our blog attributes to dedicated platforms of this kind are structured interview kits, scorecard-based candidate evaluation, and reporting on source quality and time-to-hire. Our ATS glossary adds the concrete workflow: a recruiter scoring candidates against predefined criteria and automatically advancing the top-scoring applicants to the next round. Read together, these sources describe a product whose center of gravity is the interview loop itself — the kit the interviewer works from, the scorecard they file, and the reporting that shows where candidates came from and how long each stage took.

content.title: From application to onboarding handoff
content.body: Our guides describe the path a candidate takes through this platform, from the posting that opens the requisition to the workflow it starts in another system once the offer is signed. It is the sequence our HR technology guide places at the center of the applicant-tracking layer, and every recorded step below is a point where one of our own pages describes the product working:
items: Job posting distribution and applicant pipeline tracking, the base functions our recruiting pricing guide lists for this class of tool
Structured interview kits that put the same questions and rubric in front of every interviewer
Scorecard-based evaluation, with top-scoring candidates advancing automatically to the next round
Reporting on source quality and time-to-hire, so recruiting spend can be read against channel performance
The HRIS handoff: an accepted offer triggers onboarding there, starting IT provisioning, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment
Cloud delivery with an API our dataset marks as available for connecting the surrounding stack

content.title: The two pricing pictures in our data
content.body: Three of our pages describe what Greenhouse costs and none quite the same way. This page records a list band of $150-200/mo. Our HR category page prices recruiting-specific tools on annual contracts rather than monthly seats, which contradicts the unit carried here. Our recruiting pricing guide then cuts the other direction: none of the platforms it evaluates carry published pricing verification, and it tells readers to check the vendor's own pricing page for exact rates. Treat the band above as a recorded figure for comparison purposes, not as a confirmed quote.

content.title: What the rankings say about Greenhouse
content.body: Greenhouse appears in more of our rankings than any other applicant tracking system in this cluster. It holds the number two position in our recruiting software ranking, described there as aimed at fast-growing startups that need a scalable platform, and the number five position in our HR platforms list. The segment pages for agencies, enterprise teams, freelancers, remote teams, small businesses, and startups all carry it at the same rank. Our recruiting ranking names it first among the entry points small teams typically start with, and separately calls it one of the strongest candidates for larger organizations.

content.title: How the head-to-head records read Greenhouse
content.body: Ten comparison files pair Greenhouse with another product. It is the recorded winner against ADP, Basecamp, Lever, Workday, and Zoho People, and the recorded loser against BambooHR, FreshBooks, Gusto, HiBob, and Rippling. Two of those pairings — Basecamp and FreshBooks — sit outside the HR category entirely, where the verdict turns on category fit rather than shared features. Inside the category the split is even, and every loss goes to an opponent with a higher recorded rating; our comparison pages do not itemize a single capability Greenhouse lacks.

content.title: Deployment and the certification record
content.body: Our dataset records Greenhouse as a cloud-delivered product with an API marked available, and that is the structural part of the deployment picture we can state with confidence. What no page in this repository records is a vendor certification: no compliance attestation for Greenhouse appears anywhere in our files. Buyers with a security review ahead of them check the vendor’s published documentation for the current position rather than infer anything from this page. Support tiers, uptime commitments, and data residency options are likewise absent from our records.

content.title: What Greenhouse is recorded as not covering
content.body: Greenhouse is recorded as a paid product, so the free-tier language our generated notes once attached to it does not survive contact with the pricing fields. It is also not a payroll or core HR system: the same guide that places it in the stack describes a handoff to an HRIS, which only matters if something else holds the employee record. Beyond the hiring loop our files are silent on module scope — no benefits administration, time tracking, or performance features are recorded for Greenhouse either way — so a buyer comparing suites should treat those questions as open with the vendor.

content.title: Who the guides point toward Greenhouse
content.body: The clearest fit statement in our files comes from the HR technology stack guide: companies hiring more than twenty people a year should evaluate dedicated platforms of this kind, and at seventy-five to two hundred employees it names Greenhouse as the upgrade path when recruiting volume demands it. Our recruiting ranking points the same way for small teams and separately lists it among the strongest candidates for larger organizations. Companies that hire only a few people a year, or that want payroll and employee records handled in the same system, sit outside what our records describe this product as being.

content.title: Basis of this assessment
content.body: This page reads back what our own reviews, rankings, comparisons, guides, and glossary entries record about Greenhouse; no one here has run a requisition through it. The rating and review count stored on the page — 4.3 out of 5 from 1,360 reviews — match what our comparison files use for Greenhouse, and the alternatives pages that list it carry the same figure. Where our pages disagree, as they do on the unit of its pricing, the disagreement is left standing rather than resolved in favor of one source.

faqs.question: Is Greenhouse an applicant tracking system or a full HR suite?
faqs.answer: Our records file it as an enterprise hiring platform with structured interviewing — an ATS, not a payroll or core HR system. Our HR technology guide treats the handoff into a separate HRIS as the key integration point.

faqs.question: What does Greenhouse cost according to this dataset?
faqs.answer: This page records a list band of $150-200/mo. Our category page prices recruiting tools on annual contracts instead, and our pricing guide says none of the platforms it covers carry published pricing verification.

faqs.question: How does Greenhouse do in the recorded comparisons?
faqs.answer: It wins five of ten pairings — against ADP, Basecamp, Lever, Workday, and Zoho People — and loses five, to BambooHR, FreshBooks, Gusto, HiBob, and Rippling. Every recorded loss went to a product with a higher rating.

faqs.question: Does Greenhouse start onboarding in another system?
faqs.answer: Yes, per our employee onboarding glossary: when a candidate accepts an offer, platforms like this one trigger onboarding workflows in the HRIS so IT provisioning, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment begin without a manual relay.

faqs.question: Which of our rankings include Greenhouse?
faqs.answer: It is number two in our recruiting software ranking and number five in our HR platforms list, and it carries the same rank across our segment pages for agencies, enterprise teams, freelancers, remote teams, small businesses, and startups.

author: Emily Nakamura
learningCurve: Team-dependent — interview kits and scorecards must be configured before the first requisition opens
whoShouldUse: Companies hiring more than twenty people a year that need a dedicated applicant tracking layer in front of an HRIS, and larger organizations our recruiting ranking names among the strongest candidates for enterprise use.
whoShouldNotUse: Teams that hire only occasionally and want payroll or employee records handled in the same system, plus buyers who need published support terms or certifications on file before signing.
